report.summary: Chunk 3 of containment.py: implements integrity label reading/writing, LowIntegrityLog class with dual-handle verification, and NtCreateFile-based append-only handle opening.
risks: _nt_open_append | high | Uses hardcoded \\??\\ prefix for NT path; may not work for all paths or long paths. | Check if path normalization is needed or if MAX_PATH is exceeded.

_label_sid_from_handle | medium | Memory management: LocalFree(sd) in finally block; but if GetAce or ConvertSidToStringSidW fails, sd is still freed correctly. | Verify that all error paths free allocated memory.

LowIntegrityLog.__init__ | medium | If _file_identity(self._verify) fails or mismatches, close() is called, which may not clean up _verify handle if it was never stored. | Review exception handling to ensure both handles are closed on any failure.
todos: Consider adding a check for handle validity after _kernel32.CreateFileW in LowIntegrityLog.__init__.
Ensure that the OBJ_INHERIT flag in _nt_open_append is correctly set for handle inheritance.

handoff.purpose: Implement integrity label reading/writing, LowIntegrityLog class, and append-only handle opening via NtCreateFile.

claims.text: The mandatory-label SID of the file this HANDLE refers to, or None. None means 'no label ACE', which Windows treats as an implicit Medium.
claims.why: Function returns None if no label ACE found (checks present and sacl, then iterates ACEs).

claims.text: The handle must carry READ_CONTROL; the append handle deliberately does not, so this is always called on the separate verification handle.
claims.why: Claim about append handle's rights not verifiable in this chunk; no code shows append handle lacking READ_CONTROL.

claims.text: Used to VERIFY a labelling actually took effect rather than trusting icacls's exit code.
claims.why: integrity_label reads label via handle; _icacls_low calls it to verify.

claims.text: Separate from label_low_integrity because the two are not interchangeable: (OI)(CI) on a file is meaningless, and labelling the log's PARENT directory Low would hand the child a writable directory next to the log -- a capability it is not supposed to have.
claims.why: label_low_integrity_file calls _icacls_low with inheritable=False; label_low_integrity calls with inheritable=True.

claims.text: NtCreateFile and not CreateFileW: measured on this box, CreateFileW asked for 0x00100004 and produced a handle with GrantedAccess 0x00100084 -- it adds rights of its own accord. NtCreateFile grants exactly the requested mask (measured), which is what lets the rights check be an EQUALITY rather than a hopeful subset.
claims.why: Function uses NtCreateFile with exact mask; comment explains reasoning.

claims.text: The share mode is FILE_SHARE_READ ONLY. Not sharing DELETE is load-bearing and was found by measurement: with FILE_SHARE_DELETE the contained child deleted its own log by path (the file is Low, so a Low process may delete it) and could then have written a replacement full of fabricated gate output. Not sharing WRITE stops the same trick via truncate-and-rewrite.
claims.why: Code uses FILE_SHARE_READ (0x1) only; no FILE_SHARE_DELETE or FILE_SHARE_WRITE.

claims.text: TWO handles are held, and only one of them is inheritable: handle -- APPEND|SYNCHRONIZE, inheritable, on the allowlist. This is the one the child gets. _verify -- READ_CONTROL, NOT inheritable, NOT on the allowlist.
claims.why: handle from _nt_open_append has OBJ_INHERIT; _verify from CreateFileW does not set inherit flag (defaults to non-inheritable).

claims.text: Reading the mandatory label needs READ_CONTROL, and granting the child READ_CONTROL is not on the table, so the label is read through a second handle whose FILE IDENTITY is proven equal to the first. Both stay open for the lifetime of the object, so the file object cannot be swapped underneath the check.
claims.why: Code stores both handles, computes identity from both and compares; both are kept open (no close until close() called).

claims.text: Called again from spawn_contained because construction and spawn are not the same instant, and a check that is not re-run at the moment of use is a time-of-check/time-of-use bug wearing a guard's hat.
claims.why: Reference to spawn_contained not present in this chunk; cannot verify it calls verify().

observations.what: LowIntegrityLog.verify checks granted access against LOW_APPEND_ACCESS but also includes READ_ATTRIBUTES in comment; the constant is not shown.

In _label_sid_from_handle, the SID pointer calculation assumes ACE layout: ACE_HEADER + ACCESS_MASK + SID. This is correct for SYSTEM_MANDATORY_LABEL_ACE but relies on undocumented structure alignment.
LowIntegrityLog.__init__ opens _verify with FILE_SHARE_READ only; if the file is opened elsewhere with exclusive access, this could fail.
